Subject: Close cadence recast + contingency steps for evaluation plan

Hi Priyanka —

Thanks again for the sync this morning. Based on what we heard from your engineering and procurement teams, it sounds like the current MAP target (go-live week of Jul 8) is at risk unless we make two small changes: (1) compress the late-stage acceptance window, and (2) sign a limited SLA addendum for the evaluation period so procurement can approve a temporary procurement hold.

Attached is a light recast I put together (MAP_v3.xlsx) with two options:
- Option A: Soft-compress acceptance (3-day signoff window) + temporary SLA addendum (30-day evaluation SLA) — target close Jul 15.
- Option B: Phased go-live with reduced scope (pilot endpoints only) + procurement approval for a limited contract runway — target close Jul 22.

Immediate asks:
1) Can procurement confirm if a 30-day evaluation SLA addendum is acceptable? (procurement@acmehealth.com)
2) Which option does engineering prefer for the pilot scope? We can ship a trimmed integration in 7–10 business days with Option B.

If procurement cannot commit to the addendum by EOD Monday (Jun 25), we recommend formally rebaselining the MAP and raising to exec for a one-week credit/extension decision. I want to avoid an informal slip without trace — so please confirm next steps.

Attachments: MAP_v3.xlsx, scoped-SLA-diff.txt.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Engineering (PM and infra) asked for Option B (phased pilot) since it reduces blast radius and lets us validate two critical flows without full data migration. The team is comfortable with the 7–10 business day turnaround for the trimmed integration.

Two notes:
- Procurement will not be able to commit to credits/extension without exec sign-off.
- If Redwood needs formal exec escalation, we need a one-page summary and tracked changes for the addendum.
